title: Tokenization variant alignment and template fallback hygiene during model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: New model variants coming through the onboarding pipeline occasionally introduce tokenizer differences (special token names, delimiter choices, and subtle subtokenization splits) that break chat template rendering and cause downstream token-count regressions. These failures show up as either silently higher token consumption in production or as template rendering artifacts (duplicated role delimiters or missing assistant delimiters). Objective: implement an onboarding-time reconciliation pass that detects tokenizer variants, auto-applies a deterministic compatibility layer (a normalized special-token map + delimiter sanitizer), and publishes a locked version pin and performance profile tied to the reconciled tokenizer. The goal is to prevent unseen tokenizer drift from reaching hosted or dedicated customers while preserving fidelity for models that intentionally change tokenization semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding pipeline detects tokenizer-delta signature for incoming model bundles and flags mismatch against Redwood canonical token spec
A compatibility transform is applied automatically (or suggested with one-click) that normalizes role delimiters, merges alias special tokens, and emits a reconciliation report

Model artifact produced by onboarding includes: (a) pinned tokenizer version/hash, (b) reconciled chat templates that pass unit template render tests, and (c) a performance profile that reflects post-reconciliation token counts
CI gating: if reconciliation is destructive (non-lossless), onboarding blocks and creates a reviewer task; otherwise onboarding continues and publishes the reconciled model variant to staging only
Regression tests for existing models show <= 1% change in token counts after the reconciliation pass for unaffected models, and documented deltas for models that changed semantics
Documentation and a console notice are created for every reconciled model describing the compatibility decisions and link to the reconciliation report
technical_notes: Detection heuristic: compare special token set, role delimiter token IDs, and average subtoken split distribution on a 10k-sample prompt corpus. Flag if Jaccard(special_tokens) < 0.95 or KL divergence of split-length distribution > 0.2

Compatibility layer: a deterministic map of aliases (e.g., [BOS_APPROX]-><|bos|>), delimiter sanitizer to coerce to Redwood canonical delimiters, and an optional byte-level fallback that preserves original token IDs for model invocation while exposing normalized strings to template renderer

Version pinning: store tokenizer hash in model manifest as tokenizer_hash and create mapping in model catalog to reconciled_profile_id. Publish performance profile post-reconciliation into performance-profiles/{model}:{profile_hash}.json
Non-destructive mode: prefer adding aliases and sanitizer rules over rewriting token IDs. Rewrites allowed only behind explicit reviewer approval (onboarding UI will show diff and require sign-off)
Instrumentation: emit telemetry events onboarding.tokenizer.reconciled and onboarding.tokenizer.blocked with metadata: original_token_count, reconciled_token_count, reconciliation_type
Config: expose onboarding toggle 'auto_reconcile_tokenizers' and threshold controls for detection heuristics in the onboarding job configuration
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging only): run reconciliation pass for all incoming models but do not auto-promote to hosted. Collect telemetry and developer feedback (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (opt-in): enable auto_reconcile_tokenizers for models from trusted sources (internal, verified partners). Add console banner linking reconciliation reports (1 week)
Phase 3 (default-on with reviewer guardrails): enable for all new onboarding with destructive changes blocked by reviewer approval. Update onboarding docs and run internal training (2 weeks)
Emergency rollback: ability to revert published performance profile and unpin reconciled profile in model catalog; CI check will prevent promotion if rollback is requested
test_plan: Unit: tokenizer-compat tests for edge cases (multi-byte symbols, emoji sequences, role delimiter collisions)
Integration: simulated onboarding run for 50 public models (open model zoo) to verify detection thresholds and reconciliation hygiene
Load: run tokenization pipeline at 2x expected onboarding throughput to ensure reconciliation step adds <= 15% latency to job time
E2E: deploy reconciled model to a staging runtime and run template rendering regression suite used by Console (template_fuzz_tests)
